newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Plenty of spark left after record week.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Plenty of spark left after record week.

text.p: Initial public offerings look poised for strong gains this week after a stellar showing last week and a furious week-long bull run in the stock market.

Last week saw a record number of dollars raised in new offerings and analysts are predicting a similar whirlwind this week. About twenty deals are on deck, including two Chinese firms listing stock on this side of the Pacific.
"It was a great week for IPOs, and a great week for Goldman Sachs," said Tom Tuft, co-chief operating officer of Equity Capital Markets at that firm.

Indeed. Goldman led the market debuts of Santa Fe International Inc and Polo Ralph Lauren Corp, the number one and two-ranked deals so far in 1997, respectively. Goldman also led Hartford Life Inc's April IPO, the number three initial public offering of 1997.
"It's a very good environment for IPOs right now, particularly for good companies," Tuft said.
Other IPO analysts say because many deals were postponed in April when demand was scant, the market was able to weed out lower quality deals, leaving better firms on the menu.

Helped by the two mega-IPOs, last week was the top grossing week for IPOs so far in 1997. Thirteen offerings raised $2.65 billion, a stunning 967 percent more than in the previous week, according to MCM Corporatewatch.

This week, 25 IPOs are on deck to raise $2.3 billion. ARM Financial Group Inc, Qwest Telecommunications and Genesys Telecommunications all look like winners, with analysts forecasting premiums of a point or more.
Qwest was founded in 1988 by railroad Southern Pacific Rail Corp, now part of Union Pacific Corp.

Qwest is building a nationwide fiber optic network for phone, fax, paging and multimedia communications that piggybacks on existing railroad systems. It recently leased a duct system running underneath Amtrak's Northeast Corridor rail line for its network. GTE Corp, Frontier Corp, and WorldCom Inc have all bought rights to use Qwest's network.
Qwest is offering 11.5 million shares to price between $17 and $20 in an IPO to be led by Salomon Brothers.
Software application company Genesys will offer two million of the 2.5 million shares to be sold in its IPO, led by Goldman Sachs.

ARM Financial, which provides asset management services, will offer 5.75 million shares for $12-$14 each. Manish Shah, editor of the IPO Maven, said the deal is four times oversubscribed and could rise two points or more at its market debut. He said Great Plains Software GPSI.O could also stir interest.
Two Hong Kong offerings could reap rewards as investors grab a chance to invest in China, according to John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.
"Hong Kong red chip IPOs are explosive right now," he said. Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated companies with mainland Chinese financial backing.
"For a week, China will be exporting capitalism to the United States -- in the form of IPOs," he said.

Plastics and resins-maker Beijing Yanua Petrochemical Co Ltd will offer 9.1 million ADRs for between $10.99 and $14.65 each. Peak International Ltd, which supplies products that handle semiconductor chips, will offer three million shares for $12 to $14 each. Both could post sharp gains.

The largest deal due this week is the privatization of Portugal's national electric company Electricidad de Portugal. Thirty percent of EDP will be sold in a global offering of 150 million shares. They should price between $20.53 to $26.39 each, according to the prospectus, depending on the pricing and foreign exchange fluctuations.
Boston Properties Inc, a real estate investment trust owned by Mort Zuckerman, has filed to raise $737.5 million in an offering of 29.5 million shares for about $25 each.
((-- Wall Street Desk 212 859-1881))
